title: How Important Is This to You
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that a great deal of workplace conflict traces back to leaders underestimating how much a seemingly small issue matters to someone else. The fix is disarmingly simple: ask people directly how important a matter is to them, and follow up by asking why. Doing so surfaces the emotional stakes behind a request before a leader dismisses it as trivial. The author frames this habit as a low-cost way to signal respect and head off resentment before it hardens into conflict.
points: Ask How important is this to you? before addressing an issue someone raises
Follow up with Why? to understand the other persons view of the world and the relationship
Conflicts often erupt because one party never learned how much an issue mattered to the other
Taking issues seriously, regardless of your own view of their size, builds trust and reduces conflict
quotes: Conflicts, large and small, are born from one party not giving an issue of great importance to the other party the gravity they believe it deserves.
When people bring issues to your attention to discuss or resolve, it’s a good idea to ask them this question before attending to it: How important is this to you?
Good leaders make whatever is important to you important to them.
The default of asking these questions signals genuine respect and interest in others and encourages people to share openly about what they expect.
By not taking the issue seriously, the other party saw your actions (or lack thereof) as symbolic of the relationship.
